text:
maya: Heads-up: after enabling the new kernel-selector heuristic in staging, we see throughput drop on an 8-GPU TP job and weird FP8 scaling issues with the KV cache. anyone seen this?
sam: saw a small regression in nightly, yeah. do you have perf traces or a minimal repro?
maya: pasting the core of the trace here — focus on allreduce wait vs compute overlap and kv restore errors:
```
PROFILE SUMMARY:
model: llama-3-like, tp=4, pp=2, bs=8, seq=2048
tokens/sec:  12.4k  (baseline 15.1k)
avg step time:  80ms   (baseline 66ms)
allreduce wait (avg):  +12.3ms
compute-util: 68% (baseline 85%)
comm-overlap windows shrunk around repeatable matmul calls at layer 14..18
kv-restore: 3 NaNs detected on shard-3 during fp8->fp16 restore
```
alberto: that looks like the kernel selector is picking the small-seq matmul kernel that has poor COMM overlap on our device topology. it picks based on flop/count heuristics — edge case for seq>1024 but <4096.
lin: also that fp8 scaling mismatch on shard-3 suggests asymmetric exponent scaling. if quant scales are not synchronized across TP shards, kv restore can underflow/overflow. saw similar once when we changed the accidental global-reduce order.
perf-bot: nightly-regressions: job/llama3_tp8_staging: throughput -17.9%, allreduce avg +12.1ms, kv-restore-errors +0.12% of steps. stack: kernel-selector-v2 enabled.
ops-bot: canary rollouts: kernel-selector-v2 currently enabled on canary-13 (3/10 nodes). no automated rollback.
maya: can we try forcing kernel choices to prove it? i'll also run quant-runner to compare per-tensor vs per-channel scaling.
sam: try env override: 
```
export RW_KERNEL_HINT=fast_small_seq
export RW_FORCE_COMM_SCHEDULE=overlap_aggressive
./run_infer.sh --tp 4 --pp 2 --seq 2048 --profile
```
that should force the small-seq optimized kernel and push the overlap scheduler to be aggressive. if perf recovers, selector heuristics are the culprit.
neil: FYI we've hit NaNs from FP8 scaling drift before — resolution was to initialize quant scales with a synchronized all-reduce at model load and to clamp restoration if scale ratio > 16.
alberto: +1 to synchronized init. also we should add an Fallback-to-FP16 path for kv-restore when NaNs appear: cheap to implement and safe.
lin: i'll add a guarded clamp: 
```
if (!isfinite(scale) || scale_ratio>16) {
  scale = safe_fp16_scale;
  kv_restore_mode = FP16_FALLBACK;
  metrics.inc("kv_restore_fp8_fallback");
}
```
maya: plan: a) reproduce with RW_KERNEL_HINT override b) run quant-runner per-channel vs per-tensor c) add kv restore guard + metric d) if perf still bad, rollback selector v2 on canary. i'll open a perf ticket and attach traces.
sam: sounds good. i'll run the forced-kernel experiment on dedicated-gpu-pool and attach flamegraphs.
perf-bot: queued: perf/trace/1825001111/fast_hint_run -> expected finish ~ 1825003000
ops-bot: if you want a quick rollback, i can disable kernel-selector-v2 on canary-13 now. say the word.
maya: hold for reproducer first. i'll post the run link in 10m. thanks all :thumbsup:
